source.citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.leaves: Usually two leaflets per leaf; disk-bearing branched tendril terminal, leaflet bases cordate, petiole 1–2 cm
records.flowers: Axillary clusters; red-orange corolla lighter within, 4–5 cm long
records.habitat: Moist woods, especially eastern Texas; cultivated and sometimes spreads or escapes in north-central Texas
records.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Shrubby climber with aerial adventitious rootlets, to 10 m or more
records.flowers: Terminal panicles; calyx teeth ca. 1/5 of tube; orange to orange-red corolla 2–2.5 cm with 5 short recurved lobes
records.habitat: Stream banks, disturbed areas, fence lines, cultivation; eastern half of Texas
records.note: Use exact source corolla measurement despite potential discrepancy with other floras; later crosscheck explicitly.
records.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.leaves: Ovate to ovate-oblong blades 15–30 cm, truncate to cordate base and acuminate tip; petioles to 15 cm
records.flowers: Few-flowered showy panicle; white corollas ca. 50 mm with yellow lines and brown-purple internal markings
records.fruits: Cylindrical capsule 20–45(–60) cm long, about 1.5 cm thick
records.seeds: Flat, 30–40 mm long and 4–5(–8) mm wide
records.habitat: Cultivated, roadsides, streams; historical escapes east Texas
records.source_distribution: Flora considers native to Mississippi Valley, cultivated and escaping in Texas
records.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Shrub or small tree to 10 m
records.leaves: Opposite or alternate, narrow linear-lanceolate entire blades
records.flowers: Terminal racemes to 30 cm; white/purple/yellow patterned corollas varying widely, some flowers sterile
records.fruits: Capsules to 30 cm long, usually ca. 6 mm thick
records.habitat: Cultivated highway and landscape plant, persists and sometimes escapes in north-central Texas; historically native farther west
records.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Deciduous shrub with looping, sometimes half-vining stems
records.leaves: Blades acute or obtuse, 2.5–4 cm, petioles 1–7 mm; glabrous in var. glabrifolia, pubescent in var. pubescens
records.flowers: Sexes generally separate; flowers before leaves; female umbels/corymbs 3–12 flowers; filament 1–4 mm (source key)
records.taxonomy: 1999 recognizes two varieties glabrifolia and pubescens; variety-specific pubescence must not be universalized.
records.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Deciduous tree to 20 m, usually glabrous in north-central Texas
records.leaves: Opposite odd-pinnate with 5–7 leaflets; leaf bases decurrent, lateral petiolules 0–7 mm according to key
records.flowers: Flowers in panicles before or with leaves, corolla absent; genus often dioecious
records.fruits: Samara 3–7.5 cm, lanceolate to oblong-ovate; wing strongly decurrent along fruit body
records.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Small deciduous tree to ca. 16 m, glabrous
records.leaves: Leaflets mostly 5 (range 5–7), often drooping, suborbicular-ovate to obovate or narrowly elliptic; key usually <6(–8) cm, 1.75–2.5× as long as wide
records.flowers: Early spring, corollas absent as in genus
records.fruits: Winged samaras 1.5–2.7(–3) cm, wing not decurrent on body (key)
records.taxonomy: Kew POWO and USDA GRIN synonymize Fraxinus texensis under accepted F. albicans; 1999 flora treats F. texensis distinct but allied to F. americana. Crosswalk evidence recorded, and separate identity confirmation for actual plants still needed.
records.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Evergreen shrub/small tree to ca. 10 m
records.leaves: Glossy glabrous blades (6–)10–15 cm, usually 6–8 distinct lateral veins per side, acuminate; petioles 10–20 mm (key)
records.flowers: Dense terminal panicles of white flowers, corolla tube approximately equals lobes (key)
records.nativity: Introduced from China and Korea according to 1999 flora
records.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Shrub to ca. 2 m, branches almost horizontal
records.leaves: Very short-petioled dark-green lanceolate to oblanceolate glabrous blades; source key length generally 2–6(–7) cm and twigs pubescent
records.flowers: Open panicle with separated whorl-like flower clusters on terminal and paired lateral branchlets; corolla tube equals lobes, stamens exserted
records.nativity: Introduced from China according to flora
records.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.leaves: Short-petioled rhombic-elliptic to ovate leaves, usually hairs on abaxial midrib, typically 2–6(–7) cm by key; twigs pubescent
records.flowers: Compact panicles; distinctly stalked flowers; corolla tube shorter than lobes, stamens exserted
records.habitat: Cultivated and naturalized, invasive understorey in native habitats
records.nativity: Introduced from China according to flora
records.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Low mostly glabrous perennial to 25 cm, spreading in patches from creeping branching roots
records.leaves: Sessile/subsessile, narrow to elliptic-obovate, entire to deeply pinnatifid
records.flowers: Solitary axillary/terminal, 5–8 mm pedicels recurved at fruiting, bright red unopened buds; corolla to 15 mm, yellow interior/red exterior
records.flowering: Apr–Jun, sometimes Sep (possibly Jan farther south)
records.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Low herbaceous/near-herbaceous perennial inferred from Menodora family key; individual treatment does not supply height
records.flowers: Numerous terminal flowers with bright yellow corollas 30–60 mm
records.fruits: Pedicels erect in fruit (unlike recurved in M. heterophylla)
records.habitat: Regional western/central Texas; habitat not separately specified in brief flora note
records.taxonomy: Short comparative note only; do not borrow M. heterophylla height, fruit size, flowering, or habitat.
records.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

modern_name_sources.taxon: Fraxinus texensis synonym of F. albicans
